en: I've spent so much time here that
there are still lots of places I haven't seen.
Oh, who are you? I don't know you.
What brings you to a place like this?
I hear a murderer named Jack
has been appearing in this city lately.
I thought a lovely lady like you
might be a target, so I came to warn you...
My, how kind of you. Thank you.
Oh, it's you? How did you find me here?
If you want to talk, let's go outside.
I'm sorry, but at the hotel I'd like to rest.
Oh, it's you again.
Whatever is the matter?
I know, perhaps you could show me the
sights sometime. You must have lived here
longer than I have, after all.
See you again at Big Ben.
Idly sightseeing at your age,
you must lead a life of leisure, but
coming to London, where I dwell,
is where your luck ran out.
note: Continues msg 341284 (#8818/#8819 '...a life of leisure, but').

en: There is no going home from this trip now.
From now on, you shall live as my servant.
Good morning. Is something the matter?
I seem to have gotten a little lost.
Where are you headed?
If I can be of help, I'd be happy to
lend a hand.
I came from Paris to see the sights.
and now I can't find my way back.
note: Continues #8753 (slice 109), which must end with a clause + comma, e.g. 'I only meant to take a short morning walk from the hotel,'.

en: Oh, is that so?
I happen to have a map with me,
so let me show you on it.
Then please do.
What a kind person you are.
Good morning. We meet again.
London is a lovely city.
I'd have liked to live here a long time, too.
I've seen the sights and made a lovely young
note: Leads into #8764 (slice 109) 'friend, too. How lucky I am.'

en: Good evening. Is something the matter?
I seem to have gotten lost.
and now I can't find my way back, you see.
note: Continues #8767 (slice 109), e.g. 'I just went out for a little stroll,'.

en: On your way home from work, I see.
London really is a lovely city.
Good evening. What a lovely night.
The night breeze has its charm, too.
This is where Big Ben is, isn't it?
Yes, this is the place.
Are you sightseeing?
Yes. It shows, does it?
I came from Paris.
London really is a big city. I'm amazed.
Yes, it's so big it makes my head spin.
I'm from abroad too, you see.
So I know how you feel.
Indeed.
note: Reply to the player's 'I know how you feel'.

en: I'm grateful for your kindness.
Oh, it was nothing.
Enjoy your sightseeing.
Yes, that's Big Ben right there.
London really is a big city. It amazes me.
I'm from abroad too, so I know
how you feel.
Thank you, you're very kind.
Thanks to you, I'm enjoying the sights.
again. ...It's so big and lovely.
note: Follows #8791 (slice 109), which must end '...I came to see Big Ben' without 'again' (as for #8792).

en: I'd love to cut out this view and take it home.
I never tire of it, however often I look.
has been seen in this city lately.
note: Polite twin of #8805 (msg 341855), after #8804 'I hear a murderer named Jack'.

en: You're such a kind person.
I know, would you show me the sights sometime?
You've been here a long time, haven't you?
What would you have me do?
Somehow... my body
note: #152 '...' follows each of #8874/#8875: 'Somehow... my body... / It feels awful...'.

en: It feels awful
I'll do anything.
Anything
So
Good morning
